name: Refuse hazardous substances
description: % of harzardous substances used relative to the total material requirements and compared to market reference

name: Refuse fossil energy use
description: % of renewable energy consumption relative to total energy requirements and compared to market reference

name: Refuse non-renewable materials
description: % of renewable, biobased, or biodegradable materials consumption relative to total material requirements and compared to market reference

name: Refuse other materials
description: % of virgin material consumption relative to total material requirements and compared to market reference

name: Avoided product consumption
description: % total number of avoided produced units relative to theoretical maximum production and compared to market reference

name: Modularity
description: Time (time unit) and number of products needed for disassembly (n)

name: Product take-back
description: % of products taken back relative to total sold units

name: Critical Materials
description: % of critical materials or materials containing CRM relative to the total material requirements

name: Shared use
description: Number of expected users by product (n)

name: Durability
description: % of time added in lifespan of product or material due to design and business choices

name: Durability
description: Average of the real durability of selected products (time unit)

name: Potential use during lifetime
description: Time of usability (years)

name: Potential use during lifetime
description: Number of possible usages (n)

name: Multifunctionality
description: Number of possible functions (n)

name: Modularity score
description: Quantitative score reflecting how easily components can be separated and replaced. High modularity improves reuse, repair, and upgrade potential.

name: Materials
description: Total number of distinct material types used in the product. Fewer materials typically improve recyclability and reduce environmental impact.

name: Number of components
description: Total number of discrete components in the product. Fewer components may indicate a simpler, more resource-efficient design.

name: Material composition complexity
description: A calculated score reflecting how complex the material mix is (e.g., multi-material composites are more difficult to recycle).

name: Number of tools required
description: Number of different tools required for assembly/disassembly. Fewer tools suggest better maintainability and easier repair.

name: Separable pieces ratio
description: Indicates what proportion of the product can be physically separated without damage.

name: Raw materials intensity reduction
description: % of reduction in materials consumption per production unit relative to compared to market reference

name: Energy intensity reduction
description: % of reduction in energy consumption per production unit relative to compared to market reference

name: Energy consumption reduction
description: % of reduction in energy consumption relative to compared to market reference

name: Waste generation reduction
description: % of reductions in waste generation relative to compared to market reference

name: Material losses reduction
description: % of reduction in waste generation per production unit relative to compared to market reference

name: Water intensity reduction
description: % of reduction in water consumption per production unit relative to compared to market reference

name: Water consumption
description: % of reduction in water consumption relative to compared to market reference

name: Reuse rate
description: % of reused products relative to total sold units

name: Product take-back
description: % of recaptured products relative to total sold units

name: Consumer awareness
description: % of second life product units sold relative to total produced unit

name: Potential use
description: Time of usability (time unit)

name: Potential use
description: Number of possible uses (n)

name: Ownership time
description: Average time of ownership (years)

name: Voidance of reuse barriers
description: Indicates whether there are no physical, technical, or legal barriers that prevent reuse (e.g., glued components, license locks).

name: Reuse potential
description: Quantitative score measuring how suitable the product is for reuse without extensive processing.

name: Costs of reuse
description: Indicates whether reuse requires costly or energy-intensive refurbishment (e.g., re-coating, testing).

name: Access to high-value parts
description: States whether high-value components (e.g., motors, chips) are easily accessible for reuse or resale.

name: Longevity extension
description: Time added in the lifespan of the product or materials (time unit)

name: Extension of producer responsibility
description: Estimated % of users with access to repair and maintenance services

name: Consumer awareness
description: % of units engaged in repair model relative to total produced units

name: Potential repair
description: % of products successfully repaired relative to total produced units

name: Repairability score
description: Aggregated metric evaluating ease of repair based on disassembly, availability of spare parts, and repair documentation.

name: Durability score
description: Indicates how resistant the product is to wear and tear over time, based on material quality, stress points, and previous service data.

name: Non-destructive disassembly score
description: Measures the ability to disassemble components without causing damage (e.g., avoiding cutting, breaking glue seals).

name: Ease of reassembly
description: Score indicating how easily the product can be reassembled after repair, based on component orientation, fasteners, and clear labeling.

name: Product take-back
description: % of reclaimed products to refurbishment

name: Refurbished content
description: % of refurbished parts (or components) in product

name: Refurbishment potential
description: % of units engaged in refurbishing model relative to total produced units

name: Refurbishment score
description: A score representing how easily and effectively a product can be refurbished—e.g., through cleaning, minor repairs, and testing.

name: Upgradability score
description: Measures how easily the product can be upgraded with newer components or firmware, promoting longer life cycles.

name: Product take-back
description: % of product reclaimed for remanufacturing relative to total produced units

name: Remanufacturing effectiveness
description: % of remanufactured products relative to total produced units

name: Consumer awareness
description: % of units engaged in remanufacturing model relative to total produced units

name: Remanufacturing content
description: Number of remanufactured parts within the produced unit

name: Remanufacturing score
description: Reflects whether the product is suitable for full remanufacturing: parts tolerance, standardization, testing compatibility.

name: Secondary raw materials
description: % of total of seconday raw materials relative to total material requirements

name: Hazardous waste diverted from disposal
description: Total weight of hazardous waste diverted from disposal (metric tons) % of repurposing operations

name: Non-hazardous waste diverted from disposal
description: % of nonhazardous waste used for repurpose

name: Overall recycling rates
description: Expected recycling rate of the materials in the product (%) at EoL

name: Overall recycling rates
description: Effective recycling rate of the materials in the product (%) at EoL

name: Recycling rate for waste streams
description: Recycling rate for waste streams (%) at the process level

name: Waste generation
description: % of residual waste

name: Reverse logistics
description: Estimated % of customers with access to reverse logistics services

name: Recycling potential
description: Estimated % of customers reeceiving recycling and composting services

name: Design for recyclability
description: A calculated indicator assessing how well the product design supports recycling processes (e.g., avoiding non-detachable parts or hazardous glues)

name: Recycling compatibility score
description: Assesses how compatible the product is with standard recycling technologies and infrastructure.

name: Material homogeneity score
description: Measures how uniform the materials are—homogeneous materials are easier and more cost-effective to recycle.

name: Hazardous substance barrier
description: Indicates if hazardous materials in the product (e.g., mercury, lead) obstruct the recycling process.

name: High purity sorting possible
description: Indicates whether components/materials can be sorted to a high level of purity, enabling better-quality recycled materials.

name: Use of easily recyclable materials
description: States whether materials like aluminum, PET, or other commonly recyclable materials are used.

name: Recycling collection rate
description: The expected or observed percentage of products that are collected and processed at end-of-life for recycling.

name: Waste diversion from landfill
description: % of waste diverted from disposal to energy recovery

name: Potential recovery
description: Estimated cumulative recovered enegy from process and product EOL through energy recovery (mega joules)

name: Hazardous waste directed to disposal
description:
Total weight of hazardous waste diverted from disposal (metric tons)
Breakdown of recovery operations (%)

name: Non-hazardous waste directed to disposal
description: % of nonhazardous waste used for energy recovery

name: Energy recoverability benefit
description: Total energy consumption of landfill vs waste incineration from process and EoL product

name: Raw materials input
description: % of new materials required for recovery (%)

name: Process data access conditions
description: Describes whether product data (e.g., technical drawings, disassembly instructions) is accessible to third parties.

name: Hardware and software access conditions
description: Conditions Specifies whether firmware, diagnostic tools, or software needed for maintenance/repair are accessible (open access, restricted, or proprietary)

name: Standardised component ratio
description: Percentage of components that follow industry standards—facilitates reuse, repair, remanufacture, and interoperability.

name: Component coding used
description: Whether components are labeled with codes (e.g., QR codes, part numbers) to aid in identification and reuse.

name: Material coding used
description: Whether materials are marked according to standards (e.g., plastic resin codes) for improved sorting and recycling.

name: Tracking device used
description: Presence of traceability systems and devices, and machinereadable identifiers for materials and components
